- When sentiment is low (≤0.5) and forecast shows a sharp upward move, reduce the forecast peak to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast overshoots a recent high by >5% and sentiment is neutral or positive, apply a downward correction to prevent overbought bias.  
- In the 10–15 day horizon, model tends to underestimate upward momentum; add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment is rising.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65) and forecast is still trending up, reduce slope.  
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is flat or declining, expect a short-term rally — increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- Avoid forecasting below 64 when sentiment is above 0.6 — model often underestimates support levels.  
- If forecast shows a spike followed by a sharp drop, and sentiment is negative, expect a rebound — adjust downward only if sentiment remains below 0.4.
